task: ADR-012 (Subsidiary Management Plan Standards and Content Contracts): approve, reject, or request revision

criteria.description: Universal three-section content contract (Intent, Mechanics, Governance & Decision Rights); strict frontmatter schema with generator, owner_role, depends_on, and route-sensitive governance_policy; eliminates circular in-file hash dependency by persisting canonical hash in Episode.metadata; deterministic word-count scope below frontmatter using Unicode alphanumeric tokenization with contractions; authentic PMBOK 8 7-domain taxonomy (Governance, Scope, Schedule, Finance, Stakeholders, Resources, Risk) under Planning Focus Area with primary/secondary mappings from closed enum; strict 3-tier precedence hierarchy (Tier A Hard Blocks > Tier B Structural Flags > Tier C Content Flags); floors and caps as flags carried forward to approve-pmp or recorded as route episodes rather than unrecorded approval at staging; bounded auto-remediation (max 2 retries, immediate stub escalation, protection of human work); transitive staleness propagation per ADR-013 §4.5; §4.2.1 defines standard-library frontmatter grammar subset (flat keys, string lists, empty flow lists [], comments, string quoting) guaranteeing zero runtime dependency on pyyaml per ADR-034 Invariant 1 and non-blocking FLAG: INVALID_METADATA parser rejection behavior; decoupled daughter ADR hierarchy starting at ADR-025.

Four real alternatives named and rejected with explicit rationales: monolithic omnibus plan standard, ad-hoc plan formats without shared frontmatter, hard system blocks on word count floors, and embedding canonical content hashes in frontmatter, plus rejecting third-party pyyaml in favor of stdlib subset.

Honest disclosure of positive benefits (deterministic linting, predictable breakout/graduation cycles, clean PMBOK 8 bridge, decoupled daughter ADRs, zero external dependencies) against negative consequences (schema rigidity on LLM generators requiring robust prompt scaffolding, word counts as proxies for depth requiring domain-specific daughter standards).
Open implementation questions explicitly disclosed: timing of automated linter execution during orchestrator draft mode, and learner policy scoring rubrics beyond word count.
